addendum: Wikipedia-led tests, addendum g: Test F, AI matchmaking of Wikipedia pages and books into the same book themes
parent_record: prereg/wiki_led_settings_2026-10-20.json; follows addenda a to f
fixed_by: Claude, for Khant Phyo Wai, who asked (21 Oct, 01:50) that an intelligent model, not word matching, sort Wikipedia pages and the books into the same themes, and that the test ask whether a significant rise of a theme's pages is followed by a rise in borrowing of that theme's books. Khant chose Opus subagents as the sorter and asked that the AI sort the books too (AskUserQuestion, 21 Oct).
question: When public attention to a theme rises across the Wikipedia pages an AI has assigned to that theme, does borrowing of that theme's books rise afterwards, and does this AI matchmaking predict borrowing better than the earlier routings (hand-checked concept pages, embedding match, zero-shot classifier)?
page_universe: Pages of English Wikipedia that were in the daily top 500 (data/raw/wiki_top_daily.json, 2016-01-01 to 2026-09-30) on at least 2 different days, leaving out non-article namespaces (Main_Page, Special:, Wikipedia:, Portal:, File:, Help:, Template:, Category:, User:, Talk:, Book:, Draft:, Module:): 84,577 pages. In addition a fixed random sample of 3,000 pages that were in the top 500 on exactly 1 day (seed 20261021) is sorted for a coverage check only (reported, never used in G2 to G4).
page_text: For each page: the Wikidata short description (pageprops wikibase-shortdesc) and the first sentence of the lead (TextExtracts: exintro, explaintext, exsentences=1), from the Wikipedia Action API at no more than 3 requests a second with the project user agent, redirects followed. A page with neither is sorted on its title alone and flagged.
theme_guide: The 242 narrow themes of data/db/taxonomy_v3/theme_nodes.parquet (level 3): code (node_id), theme label, middle label, broad label, and up to 8 member terms in stored order. Saved as prereg/addenda_wiki_led/2026-10-21_g_theme_guide.tsv and fingerprinted in prereg/README.md before any sorting.
books: The 20,000 Seattle works with the most checkouts in data/db/taxonomy_v3/spl_works.parquet (checkouts_total; at least 955 loans). This choice uses loans of the whole period, a look-ahead in the choice of books (as in Test A), disclosed. Text per book: title, creator, up to 10 librarian subject headings, up to 10 digital subject tags, and the first 300 characters of a linked Goodreads description where present.

sorter.who: Opus subagents of this Claude Code session, each with the fixed instructions (pages: 2026-10-21_g_prompt_pages.md; books: 2026-10-21_g_prompt_books.md; both fingerprinted) and the theme guide, each sorting one chunk of 2,500 items in a fixed random order (seed 20261021), writing tab-separated lines. Lines with codes not in the guide are re-asked once; what remains invalid is dropped and counted.
sorter.reliability: A second, independent Opus pass sorts a fixed random 1,000 pages and 500 books (seed 20261022). Reported: agreement of the first theme, any overlap, and agreement on none.
sorter.prompt_examples: The pages instructions name three examples (The Bear, Ocean's 8, Adolescence). These three pages are left out of every validation score.

G1_validation: An independent Opus judge with its own instructions (2026-10-21_g_prompt_judge.md, fingerprinted) labels 400 pages: up to 100 hard cases (pages of data/db/interest/wiki/review_title_confusion.csv, adaptation pages of data/db/wiki_led/adaptations.parquet that reached the top 500, and pages where the stored embedding and zero-shot routings disagree) and the rest random from the universe (seed 20261023). Reported for the AI sorter, the zero-shot classifier routing (p >= 0.50) and the embedding routing (cosine >= 0.70) of the benchmark: the share of routed page-theme pairs the judge also gives (precision), the share of the judge's pairs found (recall), and on pages the judge marks as having a misleading title, the share each method routes to a theme the judge does not give. Descriptive; nothing is tuned on it.

theme_attention_series.weights: Confidence 3, 2, 1 count 1.0, 0.6 and 0.3; narrow themes from the page assignments; middle themes as the sum of their narrow themes.
theme_attention_series.S1_top500: Weekly sum over a theme's pages of their user views on the days they were in the daily top 500, times the weight, divided by all English Wikipedia user views that week (the totals used by the benchmark in data/db/interest/wiki/).
theme_attention_series.S2_full: The same with each page's full daily user views (Wikimedia REST per-article, all-access, user, 2015-07-01 to 2026-09-30, at most 3 requests a second, one downloader at a time) for every page assigned with confidence 2 or 3; if more than 40,000 such pages, the 40,000 with the most top-500 days.

demand_panels.a_headings_all: The existing theme demand panel (data/db/study3/demand_panel.parquet), built from librarian subject headings on all works.
demand_panels.b_ai_20k: Theme shares per format and month from the 20,000 AI-sorted works: each work's weights (3, 2, 1 as above, scaled to sum to 1 over its themes) times its loans, divided by all loans of those 20,000 works in that format and month; excluded months as in the benchmark.
demand_panels.c_headings_20k: The same 20,000 works with their librarian-heading theme strengths (data/db/taxonomy_v3/work_theme.parquet), same denominator, so that b and c differ only in who sorted the books.

tests.G2_matchmaking_primary: Lasting rises in S2 (S1 if S2 is not complete by 2026-10-22 18:00 +07) detected per theme with the Chapter 6 detector and settings (1.5 times the normal level of the previous 26 weeks for 4 weeks or more, the study3 code and record), and the effect on borrowing in months 0 to 2 against the theme's own trend and against the synthetic control, pooled, as in Chapter 6, for panel a. Decision: the pooled months 0 to 2 effect has a 95% interval above 0. Reported beside the hand-checked concept-page result of Chapter 6. Secondary: the same for panels b and c, and for rises of 1 to 2 weeks.
tests.G3_forecasting: On the benchmark's main rows (36,081 forecasts, printed books and ebooks, horizon 1): Chronos-2 with the S2 series (and with S1) as input, against Chronos-2 alone, with the concept pages, and with the zero-shot routing, AvgRelMAE and rank correlation with the benchmark's category bootstrap (2,000 draws) and paired differences. Decision: Chronos-2 + S2 minus Chronos-2 alone has an interval below 0. Also a Wikipedia-only theme ranking with no fitting: each theme's monthly change in S2 (log), ranked within origin, format and level groups against the actual change of borrowing (the Test C measure).
tests.G4_books_side: G2 and the Wikipedia-only ranking of G3 on panels b and c: does matchmaking work better when the same AI sorted both pages and books? Descriptive with intervals.

time_rules: If sorting is not complete by 2026-10-22 18:00 +07, G2 to G4 run on the chunks that are complete and the coverage is reported. Nothing is rerun after a result is seen except to fix a coding error, which is logged in prereg/DEVIATIONS.md.
seen_before_fixing: All earlier results: the benchmark (routing changed Chronos-2 by at most 0.6%; the zero-shot classifier removed some word-match mistakes but did not help forecasts), Chapter 6 (about 9 to 11% more borrowing in months 0 to 2 after lasting rises of hand-checked concept pages), Tests A to E and their corrections, robustness and the examiner review; the counts of the page universe (139,161 pages, 84,577 on 2 days or more) and of the theme nodes (19, 86, 242); the loan cut-off of the 20,000 books (955). No AI sorting, no S1 or S2 series and no G result exists.
